en: PSB Ms. or. sim. 1504 [= NGMPP X 1504/1], 43 folios, 21.5 x 5 cm; palm-leaf manuscript; private property of Śrī Hemrāj Śākyavaṃśa, Patan.
The Devanāgarī manuscript copy is in the possession of Dr. Gustav Roth, Göttingen.
Homage to the glorious Hevajra!
Having prostrated to the Lord Hevajra, the sole vow of all phenomena,
I shall here set forth the procedure for external worship according to the oral tradition.

The mantra-practitioner, possessing the yoga of Śrī Hevajra, having recited "I am Śrī Heruka" three times, at dawn or at an appropriate occasion, places his hand upon a portion of ground where sweeping and other preparations have been made, and recites:
*oṃ rakṣa 2 hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā*.

Having thus performed the protection of the place, the self, and the yoga, one should there prepare a square mandala using a fragrant pill made of the five nectars and so forth, while visualizing the respective sites through resolute conviction (*adhimokṣa*). Reciting "pīṭha upapīṭha kṣetra upakṣetra chandoha upacchandoha melāpaka upamelāpaka pīlava upapīlava śmaśāna upaśmaśāna," and having drawn the *dharmodayā* in the center, one should consecrate the lines with the mantra:
*oṃ vajra khe hūṃ*.
Oṃ surekhe, may all the Tathāgatas empower this, svāhā! With these words, one should offer a single flower in the center of the maṇḍala.
Then, one should meditate upon the vajra as the bindus of the sun and moon.

Then, having projected from the cloth [painting] the Blessed One Avalokita with sixteen arms, surrounded by eight goddesses, who has been summoned by the syllable *hūṃ*, one should first perform the offering of water for the feet and so forth. Then, one should give him a flower produced from the syllable *hūṃ* and consecrated with the three syllables, reciting:
"Oṃ āḥ, to Hevajra, vajra-flower, hūṃ hūṃ svāhā," while [the deity] is in the center.
Thus one should offer the first flower to the Blessed One.
Again, with the three syllables:
Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.
Then: Oṃ deva picu vajra hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā. Again:
Oṃ vajrakartari hevajrāya hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā.
In front of her: *Oṃ āḥ nairātmyāyai vajrapuṣpe aṃ hūṃ svāhā*.
Having thus performed the worship, [proceed].
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ by means of this. Again.
Oṃ aṃ svāhā.
Then: Oṃ a ā i ī u ū ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ e ai o au aṃ svāhā.
One should worship with these two upon the heads of both:
Oṃ Āḥ Akṣobhyāya vajrapuṣpe hūṃ hūṃ svāhā.
In the petals of the eastern and other directions:
*oṃ āḥ gaurye vajrapuṣpe gaṃ hūṃ svāhā | oṃ gauri hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā |*
Oṃ āḥ cauryai vajrapuṣpe caṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ cauri hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ āḥ vettālyai vajrapuṣpe vaṃ hūṃ svāhā |
Oṃ vettāli hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ āḥ ghasmaryai vajrapuṣpe ghaṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ ghasmari hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā |
In the petals of the intermediate directions, beginning with the northeast: Oṃ āḥ pukkasī vajrapuṣpe puṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ pukkasi hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā ||
Oṃ āḥ, to Śavarī, vajra-flower, śaṃ hūṃ svāhā!
Oṃ śavari hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ āḥ caṇḍālyai vajrapuṣpe caṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ caṇḍāli hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā ||
Oṃ āḥ ḍombī vajrapuṣpe ḍaṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ ḍombī hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | One should worship the eight cremation grounds outside the maṇḍala.
In the cardinal directions beginning with the east and in the intermediate directions beginning with the northeast:
Oṃ āḥ caṇḍogrāya vajrapuṣpe caṃ hūṃ svāhā.
Oṃ āḥ karaṅkabhīṣaṇāya vajrapuṣpe kaṃ hūṃ svāhā.
Oṃ āḥ jvālākulāya vajrapuṣpe jvāṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ āḥ gaṅkarāya vajrapuṣpe gaṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ āḥ lakṣmīvanāya vajrapuṣpe laṃ hūṃ svāhā |
Oṃ āḥ, to the one with the loud laugh, O vajra-flower, aṃ hūṃ svāhā!
Oṃ āḥ, to the one with the sound of "kili-kila," vajra-flower, kiṃ hūṃ svāhā!
Oṃ āḥ, to the one of terrible darkness, vajra-flower, ghoṃ hūṃ svāhā!
Thereafter, one should worship the Blessed One with the eight-line mantras:
*oṃ aṣṭānanāya hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā* | *oṃ piṅgordhvakeśavartmane hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā* |
Oṃ, to the one with twenty-four eyes, hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, to the one with sixteen arms, hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ, to the one whose body is like a black cloud, hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, to the one who wears many garlands of skulls, hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, to the one with a bloated and cruel mind, hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, to the one with fangs like a half-moon, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

Thereafter, one should worship with the garland-mantra (*mālāmantra*): Oṃ! To the eight-faced one, whose upward-pointing hair is tawny and curled, who has twenty-four eyes and sixteen arms, whose body is like a dark rain-cloud, who wears many garlands of skulls, whose mind is fierce and inflated, and who has fangs like a half-moon: slay, slay! Cause [them] to be done, cause [them] to be done! Threaten, threaten! Dry up, dry up! The seven oceans! Bind, bind! The eight *nāgas*! Seize, seize! The enemies! Ha hā hi hī hu hū he hai ho hau haṃ haḥ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ!
Oṃ, with the most graceful and charming gestures of all the Tathāgatas, I bow to the Blessed One: Jaḥ Hūṃ Vaṃ Hoḥ! O Lord, accept this handful of flowers, Hoḥ!
Having thus offered the handful of flowers, one should pay homage:
Oṃ, to the mass of the spreading clouds of worship of all the Tathāgatas... [raha]hīmāṃ gaganakaṃ hūṃ (? from all sides, svāhā!
The Empowerment of Worship:
Homage to you, Hevajra, the subduer of Māras and the afflictions of Māra,
who bears a body whose very nature is inseparable from the [four] immeasurables.
Having thus paid homage and performed the confession of misdeeds and so forth according to one's ability, one should recite the aspiration prayer.
May I be born into a noble family, free from madness, a holder of the commitments, a teacher of Hevajra, compassionate, and devoted to the guru, in birth after birth.
May I, with hands ringing the vajra and bell, be a reciter of the profound Dharma;
may I be one who partakes of the seminal essence of women in birth after birth.
Then, for the purpose of completing any deficient or excessive rites, one should recite the hundred-syllable mantra.
Following that: Oṃ.
The welfare of all sentient beings has been accomplished for you, and the boon has been granted according to your request; go now to the realm of the Buddhas, and return once more.
Having dismissed it with "Oṃ mur," one should cause that wheel to enter into oneself.

In the Nairātmyā [mandala] as well, having likewise drawn the mandala, one should worship—as before—the goddess who has been drawn by the rays of light from the black syllable *KṢAṂ* situated upon the moon and sun at the center of a multicolored lotus (*viśvadalakamala*) within the mandala. Through the transformation of the seed-syllable, one visualizes Nairātmyā in the center: black in color, extremely fierce, crowned with Akṣobhya, seated in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*) upon the sun at the heart of a corpse, and possessing the nature of the three beings (*trisattva*). Having established the assembly of deities in their respective places, one should worship her first with the three-syllable mantra, and then—
Oṃ āḥ nairātmye vajrapuṣpe aṃ hūṃ svāhā.
Again,
with this: Oṃ āḥ hūṃ svāhā.
Thereafter: Oṃ aṃ svāhā. Thereafter...
Oṃ a ā i ī u ū ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ e ai o au aṃ svāhā.
By this [statement].
At the head: Oṃ āḥ Akṣobhyavajrapuṣpe hūṃ hūṃ svāhā.
In the directions starting from the east of the first enclosure, proceeding clockwise:
Oṃ āṃ vajre hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ gauri hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā ||
Oṃ īṃ vāriyogini hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ ūṃ vajraḍākinī hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā.
In the four directions of the second outer enclosure:
Oṃ =ḷṃ Gaurī hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ eṃ Caurī hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā |
Oṃ aiṃ vettāli hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ oṃ ghasmari hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā ||
In the outer enclosure, in the corners beginning with the northeast:
Oṃ ūṃ pukkasi hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ ṛṃ śavari hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā |
Oṃ =ṛṃ Caṇḍāli hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā.
oṃ =ḷṃ ḍombi hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā ||
Vajrā is in the first enclosure and Gaurī is in the second enclosure; between these two is:
Oṃ auṃ bhūcari hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā.
Vāriyoginī is in the first enclosure and Vettālī is in the second enclosure.
Between these two is: Oṃ aṃ khecarī hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā.
Thereafter, according to the sequence of the worshiped maṇḍala, are the recitation mantras for Vajra and the others:
Oṃ āḥ svāhā;
Oṃ +ṃ svāhā.
Oṃ īṃ svāhā | Oṃ oṃ svāhā | Oṃ ḷṃ svāhā |
Oṃ eṃ svāhā | Oṃ aiṃ svāhā | Oṃ oṃ svāhā |
Oṃ ūṃ svāhā | Oṃ ṛṃ svāhā | Oṃ ṝṃ svāhā |
Oṃ =ḷṃ svāhā | Oṃ auṃ svāhā | Oṃ aṃ svāhā |
One should worship with these in due order. Furthermore, one should perform everything as in the Hevajra maṇḍala.
[41] "She is Lakṣmī, you are Kṣamā; she is Awakening, you are the supernatural power of the virtuous."

You are loving-kindness, you are compassion, you are sympathetic joy, and you are the goddess equanimity; you alone are the state of peace, you are called suchness, the state of the Tathāgatas, and the Perfection of Wisdom— to you, whose body is the universe, [homage from all sides].
"Having prostrated to Śeṣa as before," thus [it is said].
After reciting the hundred-syllable mantra, the *samayagītikā* should be recited:
"kollaïre ṭṭhia boleti."
Having recited the empowerment and the expressions of compassion, one should dismiss [the deities].

By whatever merit has been acquired by me through this compendium for the sake of remembering the ritual of external worship, may this world become a supreme vessel for the true worship of the Sugatas.
The concise ritual procedure for the worship of Hevajra is completed. || O ||
May there be auspiciousness for all beings through these teachings.
Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṃgha.
